output.summary: Two signature changes with their callers: formatPrice gains a required currency parameter and tax gains an optional rate parameter. Each formatPrice caller now passes 'USD', and the two tax callers in orders.py and refunds.py pass 0.2. Unrelated edits are a config currency change to EUR, a text change in legacyLabel, and a changed argument in calc.py's Calc.tax call. Check that 'USD' and 0.2 are the intended values, and that the EUR config change is intended.

groups.title: formatPrice gains a currency parameter
groups.description: The definition takes a currency and returns it as a prefix. Read this first: every caller in the next group depends on it.

groups.title: Callers pass 'USD' to formatPrice
groups.description: Checkout, invoice, receipt and the aliased caller now pass 'USD'. Check that none should use another currency. aliasCaller reaches formatPrice through a re-export.

groups.title: tax gains an optional rate parameter
groups.description: The default rate stays 0.1, so calls without a rate are unchanged. Check that the default is still the intended rate.

groups.title: Callers pass a 0.2 rate to tax
groups.description: order_total and refund now pass 0.2 explicitly. Check that 0.2 is the intended rate for both.

groups.title: Unrelated edits
groups.description: These changes do not follow from formatPrice or tax. The method call in viaMethod and the Calc.tax call in use_calc name the same functions but are different symbols. The config currency change and the legacyLabel text change have no code link to the others. Confirm each is intended.

edgeVerdicts.reason: viaMethod calls f.formatPrice on a Fmt instance, which is the Fmt.formatPrice method in fmt.ts, not the changed formatPrice function in price.ts.
use_calc calls the tax method on a Calc() instance, which is Calc.tax in calc.py, not the module-level tax function in tax.py.
